findings.text: Debugger address argument parser accepts a symbol name or numeric address with optional signed offset, plus environment variable and register forms. It enforces a permission gate, consumes one or more argument slots, and optionally returns the resolved address, the offset from the containing symbol start, and the parsed name.

Small utilities convert a textual argument to an unsigned value, verify that current debugger registers exist with a diagnostic otherwise, duplicate a string with a caller chosen allocation type, and emit conditional debug output only when a mask test passes.

Symbol services resolve a name to an address, map an address back to the nearest symbol with module attribution defaulting to the core kernel, and print an address with optional numeric value, module bracket, name, offset, size and spacing controls driven by a punctuation mask.

Core symbol directory offers name to address lookup and address to name lookup with size, offset, module name and build identifier outputs. Name search is ordered before module search, while reverse search prefers core kernel addresses and then falls through to module, BPF and ftrace providers.

Module symbol services resolve names globally or within a named module, locate the module owning an address subject to cached range checks, and find the closest preceding named symbol within the containing memory region while deriving size and offset from neighboring symbols.

Debugger command registry rejects duplicate names with a diagnostic and otherwise appends to a global list. Macro definition mode appends statements to the pending macro, or finalizes and registers the macro when the terminator word arrives, and reports unimplemented status when no macro is active.

Output filter parser recognizes a pipe segment introducing a search pattern, supports quoted patterns containing spaces and optional start and end anchors, validates nonemptiness and length bounds, stores the pattern globally and increments a filtering flag.

Remote debugger packet handlers select current and continue threads from hexadecimal identifiers, install or remove software and hardware breakpoints after validating type and address fields, pass through selected exception signals including a detach variant that clears breakpoints, and report failures with error packets.

Address parsing requires the cursor to be within bounds, splits an embedded plus or minus before symbol resolution, prefers exact symbol match over numeric conversion, always attempts nearest symbol attribution for offset reporting, and treats a following separate sign token as an offset only when present.

Name lookup rejects empty input, binary searches a sorted name index, then expands to the full duplicate range and returns the first match address. Reverse lookup binary searches sorted addresses, rewinds to the first alias, derives size from the next distinct address or section end, and preinitializes outputs to empty and null.

Reverse module search only considers regions containing the address, skips undefined and unnamed or mapping symbols, selects the greatest symbol value not exceeding the target and the smallest value above it, and reports size and offset as differences. Core reverse search discards far matches beyond a large threshold and very low addresses.

Module name lookup supports a colon qualified form that restricts search to one module and an unqualified form that scans all formed modules in list order. Module owning an address is null outside cached ranges and null for unformed entries, with a consistency check that the address lies within the found module.

Software breakpoint installation validates the address, rejects duplicates at the same address, prefers reusing a removed slot at the same address over allocating a fresh undefined slot, marks the chosen slot as set with breakpoint type and address, and fails when the table is full. Removal only succeeds for a set entry at the address.

Thread selection fails for unknown positive identifiers while zero clears the continue thread. Breakpoint packets require comma separated address and length fields in hexadecimal, gate hardware types on architecture support and capability flags, and dispatch software versus hardware install or remove based on the leading packet character and type digit.

Macro finalization only registers when the statement list is nonempty. Command registration preserves insertion order. Grep parsing requires the segment to start with a pipe, skips blanks, requires a grep keyword, strips trailing newline, handles quoted patterns and anchors, and silently ignores empty results after anchor stripping.

Module list traversals and kallsyms pointer dereferences execute under read copy update protection, using scoped guards in lookup paths and list iteration helpers that accept a lockdep held annotation for the module mutex.

Name lookup in modules explicitly avoids mutex acquisition, relying solely on read copy update protection, as noted for use in fragile contexts. Address owning lookup similarly relies on read copy update without additional locking in the shown fragments.

Debugger symbol record as observed carries a start address, an end address, a name pointer and a module name pointer. Callers zero the record before filling, derive end from start plus size, derive start from address minus offset, and substitute a core kernel label when module attribution is absent.

Module record as observed exposes a name, a state compared against formed versus unformed values, a kallsyms pointer yielding a symbol table count and entries with section index, and per type memory bases with sizes. Symbol values and names are obtained through accessor helpers rather than direct arithmetic in callers.

Breakpoint table entries as observed carry a state among undefined, set and removed, a type set to breakpoint on install, and an address. Debugger session state as observed carries numeric thread identifiers, register context for thread resolution, a pass exception flag, and stored current and continue thread pointers.

Breakpoint slot lifecycle moves from undefined to set on install, from set to removed on removal, and from removed back to set when reinstalling the same address. Duplicate install while set is an error, removal while not set is not found, and install with no undefined or reusable removed slot reports capacity exhaustion.

Macro definition mode uses a progress flag cleared on terminator receipt. Grep filtering uses a counter incremented on each successful parse with global pattern and anchor flags overwritten. Exception pass handling rewrites the incoming packet to continue or detach, sets a pass flag, and on detach clears all breakpoints and marks the session disconnected.

Public entry points observed are the debugger address parser for command arguments, the name and address lookup routines for core and module symbols, the module owning query, the command registration routine, and the remote packet handlers for thread, task, breakpoint and exception decisions plus software breakpoint install and remove.

Address parsing modifies the caller argument string in place to split offsets, so callers must provide mutable storage. Nearest symbol attribution uses a shared static name buffer, which is not reentrant. Far matches beyond a large offset are discarded and reported as no symbol, and very low addresses are rejected without lookup.

Two definitions of the module find helper are present, one scanning the global list and one consulting a latch tree, implying configuration dependent selection that callers cannot distinguish from the name alone. Reverse lookup guarantees an empty output string even when callers ignore the return status, requiring callers to handle empty results.

Register value form is explicitly unimplemented and returns not implemented after verifying register context. Missing register context produces a diagnostic and a bad register status. Macro statement allocation and string duplication can fail, with null propagation or not implemented status and a diagnostic for the macro case.

Observed thresholds are a low address cutoff at 4096 that bypasses lookup and a far symbol cutoff at eight mebibytes that invalidates reverse matches. Symbol name buffers use a shared maximum length, module qualified names limit the module part length, and breakpoint capacity is bounded by a table maximum.

Observed syntax markers are dollar for environment variables, percent for registers, plus and minus for offsets, colon separating module and symbol, pipe introducing grep filtering with quote and anchor characters. Observed state names include formed versus unformed module states and undefined, set and removed breakpoint states plus distinct debugger status codes for permission, count, format, integer, register and unimplemented conditions.
